query: For the paper "How multilingual is Multilingual BERT?" (arXiv: 1906.01502), answer this question: What evaluation metrics are used?

drafts: The paper reports accuracy for POS tagging [5] and F1 scores for NER [22]. The passages do not establish the complete set of evaluation metrics used in the paper beyond these two [5][22].

requirements.answer_quote: The paper reports accuracy for POS tagging [5] and F1 scores for NER [22]. The passages do not establish the complete set of evaluation metrics used in the paper beyond these two [5][22].
requirements.reason: 回答给出了论文使用的评价指标：POS 任务用 accuracy，NER 任务用 F1；两处均有本地引文支持（[5] 明确“achieving over 80% accuracy”，[22] 明确“NER F1 results”）。同时明确指出无法确认除这两项之外的完整指标集合，属于对实际证据缺口的恰当说明。subject 正确（论文 1906.01502 的 POS/NER 实验），指标与单位无误，引用均来自该论文而非无关来源。

citations.quote: We perform POS experiments using Universal De- pendencies (UD) (Nivre et al., 2016) data for 41 languages.3 We use the evaluation sets from Ze- man et al. Table 2 shows M-BERT zero- shot results for four European languages. We see that M-BERT generalizes well across languages, achieving over 80% accuracy for all pairs.

(2016) 90.94 78.76 81.74 85.75 EN-BERT 91.07 73.32 84.23 81.84 Table 3: NER F1 results ﬁne-tuning and evaluating on the same language (not zero-shot transfer). performance using EN-BERT depends directly on word piece overlap: the ability to transfer dete- riorates as word piece overlap diminishes, and F1 scores are near zero for languages written in differ- ent scripts.
